stops.script: Namaste. Put your phone in your pocket, and let's walk. This sacred site is rooted in Vedic and Puranic traditions. The temple complex was established during the Mahabharata period. The idol dates back to the Satya Yuga. The history of Ujjain reaches back to the Ramayan. Lord Ram visited with Goddess Sita Mata. He performed Pind-daan for his father. In 1234, Iltutmish raided Ujjain and destroyed this temple complex.

Namaste. Put your phone in your pocket, and let's walk. We are approaching the Bade Ganesh Ka Mandir in Ujjain. This temple is located near the entrance. You will see the magnificent and unusually large idol of Lord Ganesha. This temple was established one hundred and twenty years ago by Narayan Dadhich.

Namaste. Put your phone in your pocket, and let's walk. We are at the Harsiddhi Mata Temple, one of the 51 Shaktipeeths. Legend says King Vikramaditya originally built this temple to honor divine feminine energy. As we approach, notice the two pillars adorned with lamps. These are special features of Maratha art from the time the temple was reconstructed during the Maratha period.

Namaste. Put your phone in your pocket, and let's walk. You are walking along the banks of the sacred Kshipra River at Ram Ghat. Legend says Lord Vishnu dribbled drops of Amrit here, making this place celestial. It is believed Lord Rama, Sita, and Lakshman visited these very banks to perform pind daan. As you reach the water, remember that a dip in this holy water is believed to rid humans of their sins. Every twelve years, this site hosts the famous Kumbh Mela.
